```{r}
library(tidyverse)

ex_cat    <- bind_rows(s1_cat, s2_cat)       %>% mutate(group = "Categorization")
ex_sensor <- bind_rows(s1_sensor, s2_sensor) %>% mutate(group = "Sensorimotor")
ex_voe    <- bind_rows(s1_voe, s2_voe)       %>% mutate(group = "VoE")

ex_all <- bind_rows(ex_cat, ex_sensor, ex_voe) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Categorization", "Sensorimotor", "VoE")))

ex_table <- ex_all %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    N                  = n(),
    `T_encode M`       = round(mean(mean_T_encode,    na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `T_encode SD`      = round(sd(mean_T_encode,      na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `RT_onset M`       = round(mean(mean_RT_onset,    na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `RT_onset SD`      = round(sd(mean_RT_onset,      na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `RT_critical M`    = round(mean(mean_RT_critical, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `RT_critical SD`   = round(sd(mean_RT_critical,   na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `ACC M`            = round(mean(mean_ACC,         na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `ACC SD`           = round(sd(mean_ACC,           na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `IES_onset M`      = round(mean(mean_IES_onset,   na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `IES_onset SD`     = round(sd(mean_IES_onset,     na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `IES_critical M`   = round(mean(mean_IES_critical, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `IES_critical SD`  = round(sd(mean_IES_critical,   na.rm = TRUE), 3)
  )

cat("=== Formal Experiment Descriptive Statistics ===\n")
print(ex_table)

# Export
write.csv(ex_table,
          file = file.path(folder_path, "descriptive_ex.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nExport complete!\n")
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# Prepare data
plot_dat <- ex_all %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Categorization", "VoE", "Sensorimotor"))) %>%
  dplyr::select(group, mean_T_encode, mean_RT_onset, mean_RT_critical,
                mean_ACC, mean_IES_onset, mean_IES_critical) %>%
  mutate(mean_ACC = mean_ACC * 100) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_T_encode, mean_RT_onset, mean_RT_critical,
             mean_ACC, mean_IES_onset, mean_IES_critical),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    measure = case_when(
      measure == "mean_T_encode"     ~ "T_encode (s)",
      measure == "mean_RT_onset"     ~ "RT_onset (s)",
      measure == "mean_RT_critical"  ~ "RT_critical (s)",
      measure == "mean_ACC"          ~ "ACC (%)",
      measure == "mean_IES_onset"    ~ "IES_onset",
      measure == "mean_IES_critical" ~ "IES_critical"
    ),
    measure = factor(measure, levels = c("T_encode (s)", "RT_onset (s)",
                                          "RT_critical (s)", "ACC (%)",
                                          "IES_onset", "IES_critical"))
  )

sem_dat <- plot_dat %>%
  group_by(group, measure) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem  = sd(value,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = group, y = value, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_pointrange(data = sem_dat,
                  aes(x = group, y = mean,
                      ymin = mean - sem,
                      ymax = mean + sem),
                  color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Categorization" = "#4E79A7",
                                "VoE"            = "#59A14F",
                                "Sensorimotor"   = "#F28E2B")) +
  labs(title = "Performance by Group (Box Plot with SEM)", x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title    = element_blank(),
        strip.text      = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x     = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x    = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "boxplot_by_group.png"),
       width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)
cat("Plot saved!\n")
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# ── Prepare data ──────────────────────────────────────────
plot_dat <- ex_all %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Categorization", "VoE", "Sensorimotor"))) %>%
  dplyr::select(group, mean_T_encode, mean_RT_onset, mean_RT_critical,
                mean_ACC, mean_IES_onset, mean_IES_critical) %>%
  mutate(mean_ACC = mean_ACC * 100) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_T_encode, mean_RT_onset, mean_RT_critical,
             mean_ACC, mean_IES_onset, mean_IES_critical),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    measure = case_when(
      measure == "mean_T_encode"     ~ "T[encode]~(s)",
      measure == "mean_RT_onset"     ~ "RT[onset]~(s)",
      measure == "mean_RT_critical"  ~ "RT[critical]~(s)",
      measure == "mean_ACC"          ~ "ACC~('%')",
      measure == "mean_IES_onset"    ~ "IES[onset]",
      measure == "mean_IES_critical" ~ "IES[critical]"
    ),
    measure = factor(measure, levels = c(
      "T[encode]~(s)", "RT[onset]~(s)", "RT[critical]~(s)",
      "ACC~('%')", "IES[onset]", "IES[critical]"
    ))
  )

# ── Nature color palette ───────────────────────────────────────
nature_colors <- c(
  "Categorization" = "#4DBBD5",
  "VoE"            = "#00A087",
  "Sensorimotor"   = "#E64B35"
)

# ── Plot ──────────────────────────────────────────────
p <- ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = group, y = value, fill = group)) +

  # Box plot
  geom_boxplot(
    width         = 0.6,
    outlier.shape = 19,
    outlier.size  = 0.6,
    outlier.alpha = 0.5,
    alpha         = 0.85,
    lwd           = 0.4,
    color         = "black"
  ) +

  # Facets
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2,
             labeller = label_parsed) +

  # Colors
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = nature_colors,
    labels = c("Categorization", "VoE", "Sensorimotor")
  ) +

  # x axis displays group names
  # Only the scale_x_discrete line needs to be modified
scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "Categorization" = "Categorization",
    "VoE"            = "VOE",
    "Sensorimotor"   = "Sensorimotor"
  )) +

  # Labels
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +

  # Theme
  theme_classic(base_size = 8, base_family = "Arial") +
  theme(
    # Facet titles
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),

    # Axes
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 7, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 7, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks       = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.line        = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),

    # Remove the legend (x-axis already has labels)
    legend.position  = "none",

    # Panel
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.border       = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA,
                                      linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.spacing      = unit(0.6, "cm"),

    # Overall margins
    plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6)
  )

print(p)

# ── Save ─────────────────────────────────────────────
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "boxplot_nature.pdf"),
  plot     = p,
  width    = 183, height = 110, units = "mm",
  dpi      = 300, device  = cairo_pdf
)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "boxplot_nature.png"),
  plot     = p,
  width    = 183, height = 110, units = "mm",
  dpi      = 300
)

cat("Plot saved!\n")
```

```{r}
library(car)

# ── Ensure columns are numeric ────────────────────────────────────
ex_all$mean_T_encode     <- as.numeric(ex_all$mean_T_encode)
ex_all$mean_IES_onset    <- as.numeric(ex_all$mean_IES_onset)
ex_all$mean_IES_critical <- as.numeric(ex_all$mean_IES_critical)
ex_all$mean_RT_onset     <- as.numeric(ex_all$mean_RT_onset)
ex_all$mean_RT_critical  <- as.numeric(ex_all$mean_RT_critical)
ex_all$mean_ACC          <- as.numeric(ex_all$mean_ACC)
ex_all$group             <- factor(ex_all$group,
                                   levels = c("Categorization", "Sensorimotor", "VoE"))

# ── Normality test ────────────────────────────────────────
cat("=== Shapiro-Wilk Normality test ===\n")
for (dv in c("mean_IES_onset", "mean_IES_critical",
             "mean_RT_onset", "mean_RT_critical", "mean_ACC", "mean_T_encode")) {
  sw <- shapiro.test(ex_all[[dv]])
  cat(paste0(dv, ": W = ", round(sw$statistic, 4),
             ", p = ", format(sw$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n"))
}

# ── Correlation test ────────────────────────────────────────
cat("\n=== Pearson correlation: T_encode vs. each DV ===\n")
dvs <- c("mean_IES_onset", "mean_IES_critical",
         "mean_RT_onset", "mean_RT_critical", "mean_ACC")

for (dv in dvs) {
  result <- cor.test(ex_all$mean_T_encode, ex_all[[dv]])
  cat(paste0("\nT_encode vs ", dv, ":\n"))
  cat(paste0("r = ", round(result$estimate, 3),
             ", t(", result$parameter, ") = ", round(result$statistic, 3),
             ", p = ", format(result$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n"))
}

# ── ANCOVA function ───────────────────────────────────────
run_ancova_ex <- function(dv, covariate = NULL) {
  cat(paste0("\n", strrep("=", 50), "\n"))
  cat(paste0("DV = ", dv, "\n"))
  cat(paste0(strrep("=", 50), "\n"))

  # Levene's Test
  cat("\n--- Levene's Test ---\n")
  print(leveneTest(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group")), data = ex_all))

  if (!is.null(covariate)) {
    # Homogeneity-of-slopes assumption
    cat("\n--- Homogeneity-of-slopes assumption ---\n")
    print(summary(aov(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group * ", covariate)),
                      data = ex_all)))
    # ANCOVA
    cat("\n--- ANCOVA ---\n")
    model <- aov(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group + ", covariate)),
                 data = ex_all)
  } else {
    cat("\n--- One-way ANOVA ---\n")
    model <- aov(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group")), data = ex_all)
  }

  print(summary(model))

  cat("\n--- Type III SS ---\n")
  print(Anova(model, type = "III"))

  cat("\n--- Post-hoc Tukey HSD ---\n")
  print(TukeyHSD(model, "group"))
}

# ── Run all DVs ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Use the correlation results to decide which covariates to include; include all initially and refine later
run_ancova_ex("mean_IES_onset",    covariate = "mean_T_encode")
run_ancova_ex("mean_IES_critical", covariate = "mean_T_encode")
run_ancova_ex("mean_RT_onset",     covariate = "mean_T_encode")
run_ancova_ex("mean_RT_critical",  covariate = "mean_T_encode")
run_ancova_ex("mean_ACC",          covariate = "mean_T_encode")
```
```{r}
#Assumption checks

#Normality: all DVs violate normality, but N=765 the large sample provides adequate robustness
#Homogeneity of variance: IES_onset, IES_critical, RT_onset, RT_critical are all violated; ACC satisfies the assumption ✓
#Homogeneity-of-slopes assumption: IES_onset, IES_critical, RT_onset, RT_critical are all violated ✗; ACC marginal p = .052 ✓
```

```{r}
library(interactions)

# Fit an interaction model for each DV
model_IES_onset <- lm(mean_IES_onset ~ group * mean_T_encode, data = ex_all)
summary(model_IES_onset)
Anova(model_IES_onset, type = "III")

# Simple slopes
sim_slopes(model_IES_onset, pred = mean_T_encode, modx = group)

# Visualize
interact_plot(model_IES_onset, pred = mean_T_encode, modx = group,
              x.label = "T_encode", y.label = "IES_onset")
```

```{r}
# Run simple-slopes analyses for all DVs
for (dv in c("mean_IES_onset", "mean_IES_critical",
             "mean_RT_onset", "mean_RT_critical")) {
  cat(paste0("\n=== ", dv, " ===\n"))
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group * mean_T_encode")),
              data = ex_all)
  print(sim_slopes(model, pred = mean_T_encode, modx = group))
}
```

```{r}
# Categorization and VoE: T_encode significantly and positively predicts all DVs; longer question-reading time is associated with lower efficiency.
# Sensorimotor: T_encode is nonsignificant for all DVs; question-reading time is unrelated to performance.
```

Assumption checks
Normality is violated, but the large sample (N = 765) provides adequate robustness. The homogeneity-of-variance assumption is violated for IES and RT, but the group sizes are similar (261, 258, and 246), so the impact on the results should be limited. The homogeneity-of-slopes assumption is also violated for IES and RT; therefore, these DVs are analyzed with regression models that include interaction terms. The assumption is satisfied for ACC, so ANCOVA is used.

Main effects (Type III SS)
Group differences are highly significant for all dependent variables:

IES_onset: F(2, 761) = 30.32, p < .001
IES_critical: F(2, 761) = 28.63, p < .001
RT_onset: F(2, 761) = 23.34, p < .001
RT_critical: F(2, 761) = 23.34, p < .001
ACC: F(2, 761) = 56.78, p < .001

Post-hoc pairwise comparisons
DV              Sen vs Cat      VoE vs Cat    Sen vs VoE
IES_onset       Sen > Cat ***   VoE < Cat *   Sen > VoE ***
IES_critical    Sen > Cat ***   n.s.          Sen > VoE ***
RT_onset        Sen > Cat ***   n.s.          Sen > VoE ***
RT_critical     Sen > Cat ***   n.s.          Sen > VoE ***
ACC             Sen < Cat ***   VoE > Cat **  Sen < VoE ***


The Sensorimotor group performs worst on every measure (longest RT, highest IES, and lowest ACC). VoE and Categorization perform similarly, although VoE slightly outperforms Categorization on IES_onset and ACC.

T_encode moderation effect (simple slopes)
The interaction model reveals that the direction and magnitude of the T_encode effect differ significantly across groups.

Categorization: T_encode significantly and positively predicts all DVs (IES_onset: b = 0.16, p = .02; IES_critical: b = 0.17, p < .001; RT_onset/RT_critical: b = 0.15, p < .001), indicating that longer question-reading time is associated with lower response efficiency.
Sensorimotor: T_encode is nonsignificant for all DVs (all p > .40), indicating that reading time does not affect response efficiency in this group.
VoE: T_encode significantly and positively predicts all DVs (IES_onset: b = 0.26, p = .03; IES_critical: b = 0.25, p < .001; RT_onset/RT_critical: b = 0.21, p < .001) and has the largest slope, indicating that reading time has the strongest negative effect on efficiency in the VoE group.


Overall interpretation
Overall efficiency across the three tasks ranks as VoE ≈ Categorization > Sensorimotor. The Sensorimotor group performs significantly worse than the other two groups on every measure.
The moderation by T_encode suggests differences in cognitive mechanisms across the three tasks. In the Categorization and VoE tasks, question-reading time appears to reflect cognitive processing load: longer reading implies greater comprehension difficulty, which in turn reduces the efficiency of subsequent judgments. In the Sensorimotor task, reading time is unrelated to performance, suggesting greater reliance on intuitive perception or automatic processing. Question comprehension is not the primary bottleneck; task difficulty may arise mainly from visuomotor judgment rather than language comprehension.


```{r}
library(car)
library(interactions)

# ── Log transformation ─────────────────────────────────────────
ex_all$log_IES_onset    <- log(ex_all$mean_IES_onset)
ex_all$log_IES_critical <- log(ex_all$mean_IES_critical)
ex_all$log_RT_onset     <- log(ex_all$mean_RT_onset)
ex_all$log_RT_critical  <- log(ex_all$mean_RT_critical)
ex_all$log_T_encode     <- log(ex_all$mean_T_encode)

# ── Shapiro-Wilk ─────────────────────────────────────
cat("=== Shapiro-Wilk after log transformation ===\n")
for (dv in c("log_IES_onset", "log_IES_critical",
             "log_RT_onset", "log_RT_critical", "log_T_encode")) {
  sw <- shapiro.test(ex_all[[dv]])
  cat(paste0(dv, ": W = ", round(sw$statistic, 4),
             ", p = ", format(sw$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n"))
}

# ── Correlation test ────────────────────────────────────────
cat("\n=== Pearson correlation: log_T_encode vs. each DV ===\n")
for (dv in c("log_IES_onset", "log_IES_critical",
             "log_RT_onset", "log_RT_critical")) {
  result <- cor.test(ex_all$log_T_encode, ex_all[[dv]])
  cat(paste0("\nlog_T_encode vs ", dv, ":\n"))
  cat(paste0("r = ", round(result$estimate, 3),
             ", t(", result$parameter, ") = ", round(result$statistic, 3),
             ", p = ", format(result$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n"))
}

# Use raw ACC values with Pearson correlation
cat("\n=== Pearson correlation: T_encode vs ACC ===\n")
result <- cor.test(ex_all$mean_T_encode, ex_all$mean_ACC)
cat(paste0("r = ", round(result$estimate, 3),
           ", t(", result$parameter, ") = ", round(result$statistic, 3),
           ", p = ", format(result$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n"))

# ── ANCOVA function ───────────────────────────────────────
run_ancova_log <- function(dv, covariate = "log_T_encode", data = ex_all) {
  cat(paste0("\n", strrep("=", 50), "\n"))
  cat(paste0("DV = ", dv, "\n"))
  cat(paste0(strrep("=", 50), "\n"))

  cat("\n--- Levene's Test ---\n")
  print(leveneTest(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group")), data = data))

  cat("\n--- Homogeneity-of-slopes assumption ---\n")
  print(summary(aov(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group * ", covariate)),
                    data = data)))

  cat("\n--- ANCOVA ---\n")
  model <- aov(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group + ", covariate)),
               data = data)
  print(summary(model))

  cat("\n--- Type III SS ---\n")
  print(Anova(model, type = "III"))

  cat("\n--- Post-hoc Tukey HSD ---\n")
  print(TukeyHSD(model, "group"))
}

# ── Run all DVs ─────────────────────────────────────────
run_ancova_log("log_IES_onset")
run_ancova_log("log_IES_critical")
run_ancova_log("log_RT_onset")
run_ancova_log("log_RT_critical")

# Use raw ACC values
run_ancova_log("mean_ACC", covariate = "mean_T_encode")
```

```{r}
library(interactions)

# ── Homogeneity-of-slopes assumption violated → Interaction model + Simple Slopes ──────────
dvs_log <- c("log_IES_onset", "log_IES_critical",
             "log_RT_onset", "log_RT_critical")

for (dv in dvs_log) {
  cat(paste0("\n", strrep("=", 50), "\n"))
  cat(paste0("=== Interaction model: DV = ", dv, " ===\n"))
  cat(paste0(strrep("=", 50), "\n"))

  model <- lm(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group * log_T_encode")),
              data = ex_all)

  cat("\n--- Type III SS ---\n")
  print(Anova(model, type = "III"))

  cat("\n--- Simple Slopes ---\n")
  print(sim_slopes(model, pred = log_T_encode, modx = group))

  cat("\n--- Post-hoc ---\n")
  print(TukeyHSD(aov(as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ group + log_T_encode")),
                     data = ex_all), "group"))
}
```

Interpretation of the interaction model after log transformation:
The conclusions closely match the raw-value analysis, confirming the robustness of the results.

log_IES_onset

The group × log_T_encode interaction is significant, F(2, 759) = 20.45, p < .001.
Simple slopes: Cat (b = +0.10, p < .001) and VoE (b = +0.07, p < .001) are significantly positive; Sensor (b = -0.04, p = .007) is significantly negative.
Post-hoc: Sensor > Cat (p < .001), VoE < Cat (p = .007), Sensor > VoE (p < .001)


log_IES_critical

The group × log_T_encode interaction is significant, F(2, 759) = 20.11, p < .001.
Simple slopes: Cat (b = +0.29, p < .001) and VoE (b = +0.19, p < .001) are significantly positive; Sensor is nonsignificant (b = -0.02, p = .463).
Post-hoc: Sensor > Cat (p < .001), VoE < Cat (p = .008), Sensor > VoE (p < .001)


log_RT_onset

The group × log_T_encode interaction is significant, F(2, 759) = 17.89, p < .001.
Simple slopes: Cat (b = +0.09, p < .001) and VoE (b = +0.06, p < .001) are significantly positive; Sensor is nonsignificant (b = 0.00, p = .692).
Post-hoc: Sensor > Cat (p < .001), VoE vs Cat nonsignificant (p = .128), Sensor > VoE (p < .001)


log_RT_critical

The group × log_T_encode interaction is significant, F(2, 759) = 16.38, p < .001.
Simple slopes: Cat (b = +0.28, p < .001) and VoE (b = +0.18, p < .001) are significantly positive; Sensor is nonsignificant (b = +0.01, p = .663).
Post-hoc: Sensor > Cat (p < .001), VoE < Cat (p = .047), Sensor > VoE (p < .001)

DV                  Sen vs Cat       VoE vs Cat       Sen vs VoE
IES_onset (raw)    Sen > Cat ***    VoE < Cat *      Sen > VoE ***
IES_onset (log)     Sen > Cat ***    VoE < Cat **     Sen > VoE ***
IES_critical (raw) Sen > Cat ***    n.s.             Sen > VoE ***
IES_critical (log)  Sen > Cat ***    VoE < Cat **     Sen > VoE ***
RT_onset (raw)     Sen > Cat ***    n.s.             Sen > VoE ***
RT_onset (log)      Sen > Cat ***    n.s.             Sen > VoE ***
RT_critical (raw)  Sen > Cat ***    n.s.             Sen > VoE ***
RT_critical (log)   Sen > Cat ***    VoE < Cat *      Sen > VoE ***


Main differences:
IES_critical: VoE vs Cat

Raw values: nonsignificant (p = .092)
Log transformation: significant (p = .008), VoE < Cat
Reason: the log transformation compresses extreme values, reduces within-group variance, and increases statistical power.

RT_critical: VoE vs Cat

Raw values: nonsignificant (p = .217)
Log transformation: significant (p = .047), VoE < Cat
Reason: as above, the log transformation has a larger effect on extreme values in right-skewed data.

Simple Slopes Differences:
DV           Cat      Cat       Sensor      Sensor     VoE        VoE
             raw     log       raw        log        raw       log
IES_onset.   +0.16*.  +0.10***. -0.04n.s.   -0.04*.    +0.26*     +0.07** IES_critical +0.17*** +0.29***.  0.00 n.s.  -0.02n.s.  +0.25**.   +0.19** RT_onset.    +0.15*** +0.09***. +0.02 n.s.  .0.00n.s.  +0.21***.  +0.06*** RT_critical. +0.15*** +0.28***. +0.02 n.s.   +0.01n.s. +0.21***.  +0.18***


The core pattern is consistent:

Cat and VoE: the slope is significantly positive in both analyses; longer T_encode values indicate lower efficiency.
Sensor: the slope is nonsignificant in both analyses; T_encode does not predict performance.
Slope values change after log transformation because the scales differ, but the direction and significance patterns remain highly consistent.

Conclusion:
The conclusions after log transformation closely match the raw-value analysis. This supports reporting the raw-value analysis as the primary result and including the log-transformed version in the appendix as a robustness check. The only minor difference is that the log_IES_onset slope becomes significantly negative in the Sensor group, but the overall pattern is unchanged.


```{r}
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggsignif)
library(patchwork)
library(cowplot)

# ── Step 1: Reshape raw data to long format ───────────────────────
plot_dat_ex <- ex_all %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Categorization", "VoE", "Sensorimotor"))) %>%
  dplyr::select(group, mean_IES_onset, mean_IES_critical,
                mean_RT_onset, mean_RT_critical, mean_ACC) %>%
  mutate(mean_ACC = mean_ACC * 100) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_IES_onset, mean_IES_critical,
             mean_RT_onset, mean_RT_critical, mean_ACC),
    names_to  = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    measure = case_when(
      measure == "mean_IES_onset"    ~ "IES[onset]",
      measure == "mean_IES_critical" ~ "IES[critical]",
      measure == "mean_RT_onset"     ~ "RT[onset]~(s)",
      measure == "mean_RT_critical"  ~ "RT[critical]~(s)",
      measure == "mean_ACC"          ~ "ACC~('%')"
    ),
    measure = factor(measure, levels = c(
      "IES[onset]", "IES[critical]",
      "RT[onset]~(s)", "RT[critical]~(s)", "ACC~('%')"
    ))
  )

# ── Step 2: Calculate means and SEM ────────────────────────────
sem_dat_ex <- plot_dat_ex %>%
  group_by(group, measure) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem  = sd(value,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ── Step 3: Significance annotations (Formal Experiment, using the previous specification) ─────
comparisons_list_ex <- list(
  "IES[onset]"       = list(list(c("Categorization", "Sensorimotor"), "***"),
                            list(c("Categorization", "VoE"),          "**"),
                            list(c("VoE", "Sensorimotor"),            "***")),
  "IES[critical]"    = list(list(c("Categorization", "Sensorimotor"), "***"),
                            list(c("Categorization", "VoE"),          "**"),
                            list(c("VoE", "Sensorimotor"),            "***")),
  "RT[onset]~(s)"    = list(list(c("Categorization", "Sensorimotor"), "***"),
                            list(c("VoE", "Sensorimotor"),            "***")),
  "RT[critical]~(s)" = list(list(c("Categorization", "Sensorimotor"), "***"),
                            list(c("Categorization", "VoE"),          "*"),
                            list(c("VoE", "Sensorimotor"),            "***")),
  "ACC~('%')"        = list(list(c("Categorization", "Sensorimotor"), "***"),
                            list(c("Categorization", "VoE"),          "**"),
                            list(c("VoE", "Sensorimotor"),            "***"))
)

# ── Step 4: Color and label mapping ───────────────────────────
nature_colors <- c(
  "Categorization" = "#4DBBD5",
  "VoE"            = "#00A087",
  "Sensorimotor"   = "#E64B35"
)
group_labels <- c(
  "Categorization" = "Concept Verification",
  "VoE"            = "Plausibility Assessment",
  "Sensorimotor"   = "Affordance Recognition"
)

# ── Step 5: Extract the horizontal legend ──────────────────────────
legend_plot <- ggplot(sem_dat_ex, aes(x = group, y = mean, fill = group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = nature_colors,
    labels = group_labels,
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title     = element_blank(),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.key.size  = unit(4, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(4, "mm"),
    legend.margin    = margin(t = 2, b = 2)
  )

legend <- cowplot::get_legend(legend_plot)

# ── Step 6: Draw each subplot in a loop ───────────────────────────
plot_list <- list()

for (m in levels(sem_dat_ex$measure)) {
  d      <- sem_dat_ex %>% filter(measure == m)
  comps  <- lapply(comparisons_list_ex[[m]], `[[`, 1)
  labels <- lapply(comparisons_list_ex[[m]], `[[`, 2)
  y_max  <- max(d$mean + d$sem) * 1.5

  p_sub <- ggplot(d, aes(x = group, y = mean, fill = group)) +

    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6,
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +

    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sem, ymax = mean + sem),
                  width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.4, color = "black") +

    geom_signif(
      comparisons = comps,
      annotations = unlist(labels),
      y_position  = seq(max(d$mean + d$sem) * 1.1,
                        max(d$mean + d$sem) * 1.35,
                        length.out = length(comps)),
      tip_length  = 0.02,
      textsize    = 3,
      vjust       = 0.5
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(
      values = nature_colors,
      labels = group_labels,
      name   = NULL
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, y_max)) +

    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = parse(text = m)) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 9, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.x     = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x    = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      axis.line       = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks.y    = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid      = element_blank(),
      plot.margin     = margin(6, 4, 4, 4)
    )

  plot_list[[m]] <- p_sub
}

# ── Step 7: Merge: five subplots in one row, legend at the bottom ───────
combined <- wrap_plots(plot_list, nrow = 1, ncol = 5, guides = "collect") &
  theme(
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.direction  = "horizontal",
    legend.title      = element_blank(),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.key.size   = unit(4, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x  = unit(4, "mm"),
    legend.margin     = margin(t = -2, b = 0),
    plot.margin       = margin(2, 2, 2, 2),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )

print(combined)

# ── Step 8: Save ─────────────────────────────────────
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "pilot_barchart.pdf"),
  plot     = combined,
  width    = 200,
  height   = 90,
  units    = "mm",
  dpi      = 300,
  bg       = "white"
)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "pilot_barchart.png"),
  plot     = combined,
  width    = 200,
  height   = 90,
  units    = "mm",
  dpi      = 300,
  bg       = "white"
)
cat("Plot saved!\n")
```
